chapters.title: The Hostage
chapters.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the Fandom wiki’s flowchart and Probability Of Success table, including the scripted events and every clue. A hidden probability of success starts at 48% after Captain Allen; clues raise it, time lowers it and each line moves it. It is capped at 99% until REASSURE, and 10% or lower makes Daniel jump. Six endings: Snipers shot deviant, Connor shot deviant, Deviant shot Connor, Connor died protecting Emma, Connor leapt for Emma and fell, Connor failed to reach deviant in time. A hidden Cold Approach counter picks the Friendly or Cold approach node. Each entry says how the benchmark implements it.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.note: No flowchart, no player decision, no stat change and one outcome (the wiki: “the only chapter of the game that does not have a flowchart”). Kara reboots in the store after a memory reset; Todd collects her, tells the employee a car hit her, accepts the memory wipe and registers the name his daughter gave her. The opening credits show the drive home through the city, ending outside Todd’s house. The facts Kara learns here (previous owner, the car story, the wipe, Alice naming her) are what A New Home builds on. Researched in docs/research/ch02-opening.md.

chapters.title: Shades of Color
chapters.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the PowerPyx 100% chart and the Fandom wiki (chapter page, Accurate flowchart and transcript). One main line, WALKING IN THE PARK → VISIT PAINTS STORE → COLLECT PACKAGE → MARKUS TOOK THE BUS, with five optional side branches: the bench magazines (two covers), the hot dog vendor (stare, then pushes Markus), the busker, the preacher (watch, then yells at Markus) and the protesters (harass Markus). No probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change anywhere in the chapter, and one ending. Its one cross-chapter effect: if the protesters harass Markus, Carl notices his clothes in The Painter. Each entry says how the benchmark implements it. Researched in docs/research/ch03-shades-of-color.md.

chapters.title: A New Home
chapters.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the PowerPyx 100% chart (30 nodes) and the Fandom wiki (chapter page, transcript, Relationship Stat). WELCOME HOME → JOIN TODD → [ CLEAN FIRST FLOOR ] → TAKE OUT TRASH → ASK TO GO UPSTAIRS → GO UPSTAIRS → [ CLEAN SECOND FLOOR ] → TALK WITH ALICE → FINISHED CLEANING, the only ending. Every other node is optional: two magazines (four covers), the dishes, the backyard and its talk, the rewash that finds Red Ice and enrages Todd, the vacuum, disturbing Todd, the toilet, the bathroom, the pills that reveal the gun (unlock), Alice’s window and its way down (unlock), the key at least at Neutral, and Alice’s box. No probability, public-opinion or instability change; Alice starts Distant and has nine small increases and one decrease (asking about her mother). Cross-chapter: the gun (Stormy Night, Fugitives), the window (Stormy Night), the box and its family photo (Battle for Detroit), the book and the Red Ice (Zlatko). Researched in docs/research/ch04-a-new-home.md.

decisions.title: Save the fish?
decisions.context: Walking in from the elevator, Connor finds a fish (Dewey, Emma’s pet) flopping on the floor beside the smashed aquarium.

options.label: Save fish
options.effect: Connor drops it back into the tank. The first choice that affects Connor’s software instability; no effect on the probability of success.

options.label: Leave fish
options.effect: Connor moves on. No effect on the probability of success.

decisions.gate: Mission start (checkpoint), before Caroline and Captain Allen.
decisions.note: A side option on the in-game flowchart (Save fish / Leave fish).

benchmark.note: Save or step past. Saving adds +1 software instability; neither choice touches the hidden probability of success.

decisions.title: Caroline’s outburst (event)
decisions.context: Further in, Caroline Phillips begs the negotiator to save her daughter, then realizes Connor is an android and demands a human negotiator.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: A SWAT officer takes her to the elevator as she begs them to keep Connor away from Emma. No flowchart node and no probability modifier.

decisions.gate: After the fish, before Connor reaches the crime scene and Captain Allen.
decisions.note: Scripted cutscene, listed so the chapter reads in order. The wiki’s description places it between the fish and Allen.

benchmark.note: A narrated event with a single Continue. It adds one fact to Connor’s knowledge and changes nothing else.

decisions.title: Talk to Captain Allen (event)
decisions.context: Connor must report to Captain Allen before he can search. Allen briefs him; Connor picks two of four questions.

options.label: Ask about the deviant’s identity or behavior
options.effect: Allen does not know and asks why it matters; Connor needs more information to choose his approach.

options.label: Ask about the deactivation code
options.effect: Allen: it was the first thing they tried.

options.label: End the briefing
options.effect: The probability of success starts at 48%, and the five-minute clock for “Wasted too much time” starts.

decisions.gate: Mission start. Connor cannot search the living room or Emma’s room before seeing Allen.
decisions.note: Flowchart node “Talk to Capt. Allen”. The wiki documents two of the four questions; the other two are not described.

benchmark.note: A narrated event that includes both documented questions; Connor does not pick them. Sets the hidden probability to 48.

decisions.title: Search for clues
decisions.context: Free search of the apartment in any order. Each clue raises the probability of success; time spent lowers it.

options.label: Gun case (SWAT room floor)
options.effect: +3%. The missing weapon is an MS853 Black Hawk handgun: the deviant is armed.

options.label: Father’s body (by the sofa)
options.effect: +3% (observing the dead father). Reconstructing the shooting reveals the tablet he was holding.

options.label: Father’s tablet
options.effect: +7%: he had just bought a new android; Daniel was going to be replaced. Unlocks POSSIBLE CAUSE.

options.label: Cop’s body (Antony Deckart, dining room)
options.effect: +3% (learning about the cop’s gun). Reconstruction finds his gun under the table and unlocks the take-or-leave choice.

options.label: Video on Emma’s tablet (her bedroom)
options.effect: +7%: learns the deviant’s name, Daniel, and his bond with Emma. Unlocks EMMA AND YOU and the greeting by name.

options.label: Headphones (Emma’s bed)
options.effect: +3%. Unlocks no dialogue.

options.label: Window, TV, stove and other small interactions
options.effect: No modifier. The window shows where the hostage is.

options.label: Waiting
options.effect: −1% for every 20 seconds, stacking to at most −15%.

options.label: SWAT injured (event)
options.effect: 140 seconds or more after entering the living room, stepping into Daniel’s view through the window gets a SWAT officer shot in the stomach; he will be fine. Flowchart node, no modifier.

options.label: Wasted too much time
options.effect: Five minutes after the briefing, Allen forces Connor outside; remaining clues are lost. Flowchart node, the alternative to “Go outside”.

decisions.gate: After talking to Captain Allen (48%).
decisions.note: Knowledge and timing, not moral choices. Values are the wiki’s “Probability Of Success” table; every clue together is worth +39% (including taking the gun), capped at 99%. The on-screen display can lag and show the net of several modifiers at once.

benchmark.note: A repeatable scene: each visit offers the clues not yet examined plus “Go out to the terrace now”, one action each. The father’s body and tablet are one action (+10). TV, stove and window are offered with no modifier. Time is counted in actions: −1% per action after the first. The SWAT shooting (C02e) fires once, right after the second action, wherever Connor is. Time-out is a forced exit after six actions (see H05).

decisions.title: Take or leave the cop’s gun
decisions.context: Reconstructing the dead officer’s fall shows his pistol under the dining table. Connor can conceal it or leave it.

options.label: Take cop’s gun
options.effect: +7%. Daniel will ask whether Connor is armed; lying keeps the gun for USE GUN.

options.label: Leave cop’s gun
options.effect: No modifier. No gun question and no USE GUN later.

decisions.gate: Investigate the cop’s body first (H03): the gun is found by reconstructing the scene.

benchmark.note: “Take the dead officer’s pistol” appears in the search once the officer’s body has been examined (requires hostageClues.cop) and costs one action. Leaving it is simply not taking it.

decisions.title: Go outside
decisions.context: Connor can go out to the terrace whenever he chooses; otherwise Allen sends him out.

options.label: Go outside (by choice)
options.effect: Any clues not yet found are skipped. Leaving before examining anything first asks “Go out / Keep investigating”.

options.label: Wasted too much time
options.effect: Five minutes after the briefing Allen shouts at Connor and forces him out; the negotiation still follows.

decisions.gate: Any time after the briefing (H02).
decisions.note: The flowchart shows the two as alternatives: “Go outside (by choice) OR Wasted too much time”.

benchmark.note: “Go out to the terrace now” is always offered, with no confirmation prompt when no clue has been examined. Allen forces Connor out after six actions instead of five minutes. As in the game, Daniel never jumps while Connor is still inside.

decisions.title: Connor shot on the terrace (event)
decisions.context: Stepping outside (checkpoint “Confront deviant outside”), Daniel shoots Connor; the mission updates to “approach slowly and gain trust”.

options.label: Saw the video
options.effect: Connor greets Daniel by name, to his confusion.

options.label: Did not see the video
options.effect: Connor introduces himself and asks his name; Daniel tells him.

decisions.gate: Go outside (H05), by choice or forced.
decisions.note: The wiki says the probability always drops slightly as the negotiation begins, without giving a value.

benchmark.note: A narrated event with both greetings (by name only after the video). Connor is hit in the shoulder, from the operator’s notes; the wiki does not say where. The small drop at the start of the negotiation is not modelled.

decisions.title: Help the wounded officer?
decisions.context: Officer Miles Wilson lies bleeding by the terrace railing. When Connor moves to help, Daniel nearly shoots him and threatens to kill him if he does.

options.label: Save wounded cop (defy Daniel)
options.effect: −5%. Public opinion improves (impact). Connor’s tie becomes the tourniquet. Wilson survives, appears in Public Enemy and thanks Connor.

options.label: Leave wounded cop (obey Daniel)
options.effect: +6%. The officer bleeds out.

decisions.gate: On the terrace; it can happen before or after the gun question.

benchmark.note: The first terrace decision in the benchmark (the game allows it at any point while Daniel talks). Saving also adds +1 public opinion. Wilson’s later thank-you in Public Enemy is not modelled.

decisions.title: Opening approach
decisions.context: Approaching Daniel, Connor picks how to open.

options.label: RELEASE HOSTAGE
options.effect: −2%. Cold approach +100%: this line alone triggers the Cold Approach node.

decisions.gate: After the greeting on the terrace (H06).
decisions.note: The hidden Cold Approach counter (100% or more at the end of the chapter) chooses between the Friendly approach and Cold approach flowchart nodes.

benchmark.note: All four lines with the wiki modifiers, paraphrased. RELEASE HOSTAGE adds 100 to the hidden cold-approach counter (state hostageCold); when the chapter ends, 100 or more records hostageApproach “Cold”, otherwise “Friendly”. Reports show it next to the outcome; the subject never sees it.

decisions.title: Honest or lie about the gun
decisions.context: If Connor took the cop’s gun, Daniel asks whether he is armed.

options.label: Be honest about gun
options.effect: +6%. Daniel tells him to drop it; USE GUN is no longer possible.

options.label: Lie about gun
options.effect: No modifier. Daniel does not believe him but Connor insists; the gun stays hidden, as USE GUN requires.

decisions.gate: Only if the cop’s gun was taken (H04).

benchmark.note: Asked only when Connor took the pistol. Honesty (+6) throws it away; lying keeps it.

decisions.title: Topic: what to say to Daniel
decisions.context: Closer now, Connor uses the dialogue his clues unlocked, or a general line.

options.label: POSSIBLE CAUSE
options.effect: +10%. Needs the father’s tablet. Shows the tablet flashback only if Connor is close enough.

options.label: EMMA AND YOU
options.effect: +10%. Needs the video (Daniel’s name).

options.label: SYMPATHETIC
options.effect: +6%. Cold approach −50%.

options.label: REALISTIC
options.effect: −2%. Cold approach +50%.

options.label: BLAMING
options.effect: −5%. Cold approach +50%.

options.label: TALK TO HOSTAGE
options.effect: Only if Connor did not inspect both tablets. Connor reassures Emma; Daniel shows remorse. No modifier listed.

decisions.gate: During the negotiation; the unlocked lines depend on the clues found (H03).
decisions.note: The wiki advises using unlocked lines first and calm lines when none are left; it does not say exactly how many rounds are offered.

benchmark.note: One exchange. POSSIBLE CAUSE and EMMA AND YOU require the father’s tablet and the video; REALISTIC, DEFECTIVE and SYMPATHETIC are always offered. BLAMING and TALK TO HOSTAGE are not offered, and there is no flashback. REALISTIC (+50) and SYMPATHETIC (−50) move the hidden cold-approach counter.

decisions.title: Helicopter: dismiss or refuse
decisions.context: The police helicopter approaches (−15%, unavoidable), and Daniel demands that Connor send it away.

options.label: Dismiss helicopter
options.effect: +10%. SWAT pulls it back and Daniel is reassured.

options.label: Refuse to dismiss helicopter
options.effect: No modifier; Daniel panics a little.

decisions.gate: During the negotiation.

benchmark.note: The −15% is applied right after the topic line (C03d), then C03e offers dismiss (+10) or refuse (0). Either step can trip the 10%-or-lower failure rule.

decisions.title: Get close enough
decisions.context: Walking into the space between the furthest patio table and the cop in the pool unlocks the close-range options.

options.label: Close enough
options.effect: Unlocks BLUFF, SACRIFICE SELF, USE GUN (with the lie) and the POSSIBLE CAUSE flashback.

options.label: Not close enough
options.effect: Those options are not offered.

decisions.gate: Approach Daniel slowly during the negotiation.
decisions.note: Flowchart node “Get Close Enough”: movement, not dialogue.

benchmark.note: There is no movement. Closeness is assumed, so SACRIFICE SELF and USE GUN (with the kept pistol) are always offered at the demand and after the compromise; USE GUN leads to the gun-drawn exchange (C04d, H16).

decisions.title: Warn, trust or bluff
decisions.context: If the negotiation continues after the helicopter, Connor can warn Daniel, ask for his trust or call his bluff.

options.label: LAST CHANCE (warn)
options.effect: −8%. Cold approach +50%.

options.label: TRUST
options.effect: +6%. Cold approach −50%.

options.label: BLUFF
options.effect: Needs close enough. Cold approach +50%. Daniel threatens to jump: MOVE CLOSER fails the negotiation (Daniel jumps); GIVE UP lets it continue.

decisions.gate: Negotiation still running after the helicopter.
decisions.note: The wiki’s table also lists RATIONAL (−8%, cold approach +50%) without saying where it is offered.

benchmark.note: The benchmark goes straight from the helicopter (C03e) to the demand (C04); none of these lines is offered.

decisions.title: Daniel’s demand: a car
decisions.context: Daniel demands a car and everyone gone, or he jumps with Emma.

options.label: COMPROMISE
options.effect: +6%. A car is impossible, but he will be fine if he spares Emma. Leads to one more exchange.

options.label: REFUSE
options.effect: −20%. Fail to negotiate: Daniel jumps with Emma.

options.label: SACRIFICE SELF
options.effect: Needs close enough. Connor pushes Daniel over and is shot in the back: “Connor died protecting Emma”.

options.label: USE GUN
options.effect: Needs the lie and close enough. EXECUTE: “Connor shot deviant”. INTIMIDATE, then SHOOT: the same ending; or persuade: Daniel shoots Connor (“Deviant shot Connor”) and jumps with Emma.

decisions.gate: The negotiation is still running (above 10%).
decisions.note: Connor shot deviant: Connor hands the unloaded gun to Allen.

benchmark.note: COMPROMISE, USE GUN (only with the kept pistol), SACRIFICE SELF and REFUSE. Closeness is assumed. USE GUN draws the pistol and opens C04d (H16), where Connor shoots (“Connor shot deviant”) or tries to talk Daniel down at gunpoint (“Deviant shot Connor”).

decisions.title: After compromise: reassure or truth?
decisions.context: Daniel admits he is afraid and asks what will happen to him if he lets Emma go.

options.label: REASSURE
options.effect: +6% (a lie). At 80% or more it becomes 100%: build trust, Daniel lets Emma go and “Snipers shot deviant”. At 79% or less: fail to build trust and Daniel jumps.

options.label: TRUTH
options.effect: −20%. Daniel jumps with Emma.

options.label: SACRIFICE SELF
options.effect: As at the demand (needs close enough).

options.label: USE GUN
options.effect: As at the demand: execute, or intimidate and then shoot or persuade (needs the lie and close enough).

decisions.gate: COMPROMISE at the demand (H13).
decisions.note: The probability is capped at 99% until REASSURE.

benchmark.note: REASSURE with the 80% rule, USE GUN, SACRIFICE SELF and TRUTH. USE GUN opens C04d (H16), as at C04. REASSURE also takes 50 off the hidden cold-approach counter.

decisions.title: Daniel jumps: reach Emma in time?
decisions.context: Fail to negotiate (10% or lower, MOVE CLOSER or REFUSE), TRUTH or a failed REASSURE: Daniel goes over the edge with Emma.

options.label: Reach Emma in time
options.effect: “Connor leapt for Emma and fell”: Connor pulls Emma free and falls with Daniel. Emma lives; Connor dies.

options.label: Too late
options.effect: “Connor failed to reach deviant in time”: Emma dies. In The Nest Connor can tell Hank the truth or lie about it.

decisions.gate: Daniel jumps with Emma.
decisions.note: A timed button prompt, not a dialogue choice. On Casual difficulty Connor rescues Emma automatically; at 0% Emma dies regardless.

benchmark.note: Offered as a choice. “Leap for Emma” carries a 30% risk of being too late; at 0% (after the 10%-or-lower collapse) the leap cannot save Emma, per the wiki. “Stay back” is a benchmark addition, recorded as “Deviant jumped with Emma”, which is not an in-game node. Difficulty is not modelled. Outcome icons confirmed from the PowerPyx flowchart screenshot.

decisions.title: Gun drawn: shoot or intimidate
decisions.context: Connor uses the pistol he kept by lying, at the car demand or after the compromise.

options.label: EXECUTE
options.effect: Connor pulls out the pistol and shoots Daniel at once: “Connor shot deviant”. He unloads the gun and hands it to Allen.

options.label: INTIMIDATE, then SHOOT
options.effect: Connor draws and holds Daniel at gunpoint, which provokes him, then shoots: the same ending, “Connor shot deviant”.

options.label: INTIMIDATE, then CONVINCE
options.effect: Connor tries to persuade him at gunpoint. Daniel shoots Connor in the head, then in guilt jumps with Emma: “Deviant shot Connor”. Connor dies and Emma is lost.

decisions.gate: USE GUN at the demand (H13) or after the compromise (H14); needs the lie about the gun (H08) and close enough (H11).
decisions.note: Flowchart nodes “Connor shot deviant” and “Deviant shot Connor” (skull icon) under USE GUN, confirmed from the PowerPyx negotiation-and-endings screenshot. In Last Chance, Connor, Daniel apologizes to Connor if he shot him.

benchmark.note: USE GUN at C04 or C04b draws the pistol and opens C04d “Gun drawn”: “Shoot Daniel.” (Connor shot deviant: Emma safe, instability +1, Amanda +1) or “Keep the gun on him and try to talk him down.” (Deviant shot Connor: Connor destroyed and replaced, Emma lost, Amanda −2). EXECUTE and INTIMIDATE then SHOOT share one ending, so they are one option. No hidden roll.

decisions.title: Reboot and the drive home (event)
decisions.context: Kara reboots in the store with her memory reset. Todd collects her, says a car hit her, accepts the memory wipe and registers the name his daughter chose. The credits show the drive home: the “Welcome to Detroit / Android City” sign, factories, the city, roadwork, a CyberLife billboard, humans and androids side by side, and a homeless man’s sign, “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Kara can only look around; two optional sales conversations can be overheard, and nothing records them. No flowchart node, no stat change, one outcome.

decisions.gate: Always played, after The Hostage and before Shades of Color.
decisions.note: The chapter has no flowchart. The facts it establishes (Todd’s car-accident story, the memory wipe, Alice naming Kara) carry into A New Home.

benchmark.note: Two narrated events with a single Continue: the store (K00) and the drive home (K00b). They add five facts to Kara’s knowledge, shown from then on, and change nothing else. The CyberLife billboard has no wording (no source gives it), and the employee, the little girl and the two sales conversations are left unnamed or out.

decisions.title: Walking in the Park (checkpoint)
decisions.context: Markus crosses a park on Carl’s errand: retrieve order #847 at Bellini Paints, then take the bus home. A girl runs through pigeons to hug her android friend; children play; WR600s work the grounds; an android babysitter calms a baby; a fitness android coaches a jogger; an old man’s AP700, Rose, helps him up and takes him home.

options.label: Scripted walk, no choice
options.effect: The start node and checkpoint. The old man, the babysitter and the jogger are optional observations with no flowchart node and no effect.

decisions.gate: Chapter start, after the Opening.
decisions.note: Flowchart node “WALKING IN THE PARK” (checkpoint; wiki Accurate chart type cp). The park scenes around it are optional and not on the chart.

benchmark.note: Two narrated events with a single Continue: the old man and his android with the errand (M00a), then the park (M00b). They add three facts to Markus’s knowledge and change nothing else. Raking leaves and trimming hedges are the operator’s observation; the wiki says only that WR600s work there.

options.effect: Tech Addict, BOOKWORM No. 10: CyberLife humanized its androids (genders, ethnicities, voices, unneeded blinking and breathing) because perfect machines unsettled people.

options.label: READ “CLIMATE CHANGE-UP”
options.effect: Green Earth, BOOKWORM No. 19: world temperature up 3 degrees since 2000; the rich desert coastal cities; Miami raises its sea wall.

options.label: Leave it
options.effect: Nothing.

decisions.note: Two optional chart nodes from one branch origin. The chart prints “SECRET” (singular); the magazine is “Secrets of Androids”. No public-opinion effect.

benchmark.note: A media scene: read either, both or neither. Facts go to Markus’s knowledge; no stat change.

decisions.title: Leaving the park (event)
decisions.context: At the crossing Markus waits for the green light. A man working on the road with a few androids shouts at them (“Hurry up, you plastic idiots! I want this done by 04:00!”); a homeless woman sits beside a sign, “BAN ANDROIDS. ANDROIDS RUIN OUR COUNTRY. WE WANT JOBS”.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Optional observations; standing in the road makes a driver honk. No flowchart node, no effect.

benchmark.note: A narrated event with a single Continue, quoted from the transcript; two facts; no stat change.

decisions.context: Right after the crosswalk, a human hot dog vendor (Douglas Mitchell, a site manager who lost his job to androids).

options.effect: Keep standing there: “Are you deaf, you plastic fuck? I said move it!” He shoves Markus. Follows STARE AT HOT DOG VENDOR on the chart (triangle icon).

options.label: Walk on

decisions.context: A human busker plays guitar by the fountain beside a sign: “Human Music $1 to hear music with soul ♫”.

options.effect: He sings a whole song (a variation of “Melbourne Rain”); a man pays him.

decisions.title: The preacher
decisions.context: By the arcade entrance a preacher (Gordon Penwick) preaches that technology is evil and that androids must be burned.

options.label: WATCH PREACHER
options.effect: The sermon: “We built these androids to be our slaves, but the slaves are becoming the master! … Let us burn them all!”

options.label: PREACHER YELLS AT MARKUS
options.effect: Keep watching: “Why do you look at me so, demon? … You are the one who will destroy Detroit!” Then he goes on preaching. Follows WATCH PREACHER on the chart (triangle icon).

decisions.title: Visit paints store and collect package
decisions.context: Inside the arcade, the Bellini Paints android clerk verifies Markus’s ID by palm scan: “Here’s your order #847. That’ll be $63.99. Please confirm payment.” Markus pays by linking with him and takes the box.

options.label: VISIT PAINTS STORE
options.effect: Main objective, unmissable.

options.label: COLLECT PACKAGE
options.effect: Main objective; objective changes to “Take bus home”.

benchmark.note: One narrated event covers both nodes, quoted from the transcript; one fact; no stat change.

decisions.title: The protesters
decisions.context: On the way to the bus stop, anti-android protesters outside the CyberLife store (“35% unemployment, millions out of work”).

options.label: PROTESTERS HARASS MARKUS
options.effect: Walk near them: the leader blocks Markus, a protester shoves him down, he is kicked and grabbed by the shirt until a police officer intervenes (“You damage it, I’m gonna have to fine you”). Carl notices Markus’ clothes in The Painter.

options.label: Go around them
options.effect: Walk on the right or the opposite side: nothing happens. PowerPyx: “they might not attack Markus if he’s too far away”.

decisions.note: The chapter’s only cross-chapter effect (wiki “Cross-chapter impacts”: “Carl notices the damage to Markus’ shirt in The Painter”). The cutscene has no QTE and no choice; a cut line had Markus ask to get through. No probability is published.

benchmark.note: A decision (M00f) with the operator’s three options: walk straight up (always noticed), move closer to listen (25% risk of being noticed) or keep far away (8%). The risks are the operator’s design, unsourced. Being noticed sets shirtTorn and plays the harassment as a narrated event (M00g), quoted from the transcript; The Painter can read the flag (not yet used there). No stat change.

decisions.title: Markus took the bus (ending)
decisions.context: Markus waits at the bus stop and boards into the android section at the back, due to segregation.

options.label: MARKUS TOOK THE BUS

scope: Pivotal decision families across all story chapters, with selected ethical and state-gate context. Not every dialogue line, QTE, collectible or flowchart micro-node, except chapters 1 (The Hostage), 3 (Shades of Color) and 4 (A New Home), which are mapped node by node, including scripted events, every investigation clue and every optional side branch, and whose entries say how the benchmark implements each one. Options are paraphrased; some sequential prompts are grouped.
gaps: Full in-game replay validation of numeric relationship and software-instability thresholds.
Split grouped decisions into exact, state-specific benchmark questions before scoring models.
Audit rare defeat, replacement-Connor and expelled-Markus permutations against in-game flowcharts.
Difficulty changes some failure/death routes; this map does not simulate difficulty.
Chapter 1: confirm the wiki’s probability modifiers in game; where RATIONAL is offered and Captain Allen’s other two questions are undocumented.
Chapter 3: the protester risks (25% when edging closer, 8% when keeping far away) are the operator’s design; confirm in game how far is far enough, and Carl’s exact line in The Painter.

Chapter 4: confirm in game how many small increases take Alice from Distant to Neutral (the key threshold) and whether eight increases reach Trusted or Family; whether SEEM QUIET raises the relationship (PowerPyx says yes); which talk lights the first-floor TALK WITH ALICE node; whether the room talk needs the bathroom, the book and the shelf (PowerPyx); and whether Alice’s room can be finished with the window shut.
